title: Grids split into multiple columns at window widths where the side rail and copilot dock have already eaten most of the page
surface: Every client-shell page (Workspace board, Search & AI visibility, Settings channels, Archive)
whatYouSee: On a 1280-pixel-wide window a client has a 288-pixel side rail, a 380-pixel copilot dock that is open by default, and roughly 550 pixels of actual page. The task board still splits into four columns of about 130 pixels each; the per-engine comparison cards still split three across at about 180 each; the channel cards still go three across. At 1024 pixels it is worse — about 290 pixels of page still split three ways, roughly 90 pixels per card — so badges, brand names and labels wrap to one word per line. Collapsing the dock is the only workaround and it has to be clicked every session.
whyItsWrong: Those grids switch to multiple columns based on the width of the browser window, but they live in a column that is the window minus 288 pixels of rail, minus 380 pixels of dock, minus 64 pixels of padding. The breakpoint knows nothing about the 668 pixels of surrounding furniture, so multi-column layout engages at exactly the moment there is no room for it.
fix: Tailwind v4 is already the dependency (package.json:39), so container queries need nothing new. Add `@container` to the inner wrapper at src/app/(app)/layout.tsx:106 and to the staff shell's twin at line 158, then convert the content grids from viewport to container variants: src/components/tasks-board.tsx:730 `xl:grid-cols-3/4` → `@3xl:grid-cols-2 @5xl:grid-cols-3/4`; src/components/seo-geo-panel.tsx:381 `lg:grid-cols-3` → `@2xl:grid-cols-2 @4xl:grid-cols-3`; src/components/integrations-tab.tsx:864 and :881 and src/components/archive-view.tsx:82 the same way. Verify at 1024 and 1280 pixels with the dock open, since the dock defaults to expanded (copilot-dock.tsx:25).

title: A client can never act on a draft — the pick/post/skip loop the intake copy promises does not exist for them, and their copy of the draft is an unformatted text dump
surface: Workspace → Archive tab (/tasks) — where the agent forms tell clients their drafts land
whatYouSee: The X, LinkedIn and Reddit forms tell the client that picking, editing or skipping individual drafts happens on the drafts themselves, in their Workspace archive. The client opens Workspace, goes to the Archive tab, clicks the tile for the batch, and gets one wall of text with every hash mark, asterisk, backtick and quote arrow showing exactly as typed. No cards, no thread link to click, no Post / Posted with edits / Didn't post / Request a change buttons. Nothing to do but read it and close.
whyItsWrong: The whole per-draft loop — the four outcome actions that train the agent, the copy-the-reply-and-open-the-thread hand-off, the LinkedIn compose prefill — is built and wired, but it is mounted only inside the asset card. The only two places that render an asset card are the staff-only job detail page and the staff Assets library, and both client routes into that library redirect client users away. The Archive tab instead opens a read-only detail modal that prints the asset's text verbatim. So the promise on three intake surfaces cannot be kept, the deliverable reaches the client as unrendered source (house rule: never render raw model copy to a client), and the outcome rows the Reddit contract calls the only copy of the client's outcomes can in practice only be written by staff — even though the server action behind them already accepts client callers.
fix: Mount the drafts readers on a surface a client can reach. Preferred: in src/components/asset-detail-modal.tsx run the same three sniffs the card runs (parseLiDrafts / parseRedditDrafts / parseXDrafts, in that order — asset-card.tsx:433-457, order is load-bearing) and render LiDraftsBatch / RedditDraftsBatch / XDraftsBatch in place of the plain content paragraph at line 211, passing clientId, jobId, assetId exactly as asset-card.tsx:712-764 does. Alternative: have src/components/archive-view.tsx open AssetCard instead of AssetDetailModal when the content parses as a batch. No server change is needed — addRedditDraftFeedbackAction and its LinkedIn/X twins already authorize with requireClientAccess. Until one of those ships, reword x-agent-intake.tsx:670-673, linkedin-agent-intake.tsx:622-625 and reddit-agent-intake.tsx:297-301 so they stop promising per-draft actions.

title: The client's Archive shows the agent deliverable as raw text with all its formatting symbols on screen — and shows unapproved drafts straight away
surface: Workspace → Archive tab (/tasks, client role) → tile → asset detail modal
whatYouSee: A client opens Workspace → Archive and clicks a tile from the X, LinkedIn or Reddit agent. The detail panel prints the whole deliverable as plain text with every formatting symbol visible — hash marks in front of "Reddit answer drafts" and "Account 1", asterisks around bold words, angle brackets in front of the quoted reply, pipe characters where a table should be. Ten drafts run one after another with no cards, no headings and no separation. The status badge on the tile reads "draft", even though the run confirmation told the client that deliverables show up here only after the Karos team approves them.
whyItsWrong: These deliverables are structured documents by contract, and staff get a proper parsed per-draft review panel for the exact same content. The client's archive prints the stored text verbatim, so the client sees the machine formatting rather than the drafts. It breaks the standing rule that unpolished model output never reaches a client, and it is the most-visited client screen after a run. Second, unapproved drafts are deliberately not filtered out of the client library, so the draft appears the instant the run finishes — directly contradicting the promise made in the run confirmation dialog.

title: "Autopilot on" stays on forever but only ever runs one batch
whatYouSee: You flip the switch, it turns green, reads "Autopilot on" and stays that way. It works through at most five of the pending items that existed at the moment you flipped it. Everything created afterwards sits in Pending untouched while the switch keeps saying Autopilot is on.
whyItsWrong: The persistent "on" state promises standing automation that no code path provides. The flag is written to the client's settings and read back only to render the switch and to make a repeat toggle idempotent; the batch runner is called only from the toggle itself, and no scheduled job looks at the flag. A client switches it on, walks away, and believes the board is being worked. The only way to get another batch is to switch it off and on again.
evidence: src/lib/actions/settings-actions.ts:96 — `after(() => runAutopilotBatch(clientId)…)`, the only call, inside the enable transition
src/lib/actions/settings-actions.ts:87 — the client-billed path likewise calls runClaimedTasks once
src/lib/actions/settings-actions.ts:38-39 — the only other read of settings.autopilot: the same-state idempotency guard
src/app/(app)/tasks/tasks-body.tsx:77 — the second and last read: `autopilotEnabled={settings?.autopilot ?? false}`, the toggle's initial state
src/lib/execution-engine.ts:466 — runAutopilotBatch: picks up pending tasks once, capped at 5
src/lib/execution-engine.ts:462-464 — its own comment: "Capped at 5 tasks per invocation to respect after() time budget"
fix: Pick one and make the label honest. (a) Wire the flag into the existing cron: src/app/api/run-scheduled/route.ts already runs every 5 minutes (vercel.json crons) and drains due schedules — add a pass that loads clients with settings.autopilot === true and calls runAutopilotBatch (src/lib/execution-engine.ts:466) for each, reusing the claim-then-charge loop in updateAutopilotAction (src/lib/actions/settings-actions.ts:45-88) so billable clients are still charged per task. Or (b) relabel the control in src/components/tasks-board.tsx AutopilotToggle (line 98) as a one-shot button — "Run up to 5 pending tasks now" — and stop persisting an on state that nothing honours.

title: "Refresh Task Map" promises a market-footprint scan; the run never looks outside the account
surface: AI Copilot panel → "Refresh Task Map" action → Strategy War Room modal (right rail, every workspace page)
whatYouSee: The top action reads "Refresh Task Map — Scan market footprint & surface operational priorities", and when Google is connected its icon changes to a globe. Clicking it opens "The Strategy War Room", which says three specialists are debating your task map live and stress-testing it against your analytics. After roughly a minute of scrolling console lines it closes and up to fifteen task cards appear on the board.
whyItsWrong: Nothing looks at the market, the web, the client's own site, or the inbox. The only inputs to the debate are: which connected social channels have nothing scheduled in the next fourteen days, the stored brand tone/visual-style fields, the client's own past engagement scores, and the list of custom agents. The company website is loaded but never passed in. The portal already owns a real web-search tool used elsewhere, so this reads as unfinished rather than a deliberate limit. Two knock-on breaks: (a) the button's own instruction text ("Scan the web and analyze our market footprint…") is dead code — the click handler diverts this one action to the War Room and never sends it; (b) every task this path creates is forced to Karos-managed, so the mandatory onboarding / re-authenticate checklist the prompt calls non-negotiable can never be produced by this button — it only exists on the typed-chat path.

title: A client clicking "New content ready" in their notification bell gets silently bounced to their dashboard

And these rows are only ever populated for client accounts — staff never get them — so this link is dead 100% of the time it is shown. This is the client's primary "your content is ready" affordance. title: A one-time 100-credit charge is sold to the client as "≈ $29/mo"
surface: Client settings /clients/[id]/settings — add-seat form and seat-limit blocker; the same component inside the onboarding wizard
whatYouSee: "This is beyond your 2-seat plan - adding it costs 100 credits (≈ $29/mo)." The button underneath says "Add & charge 100 credits". The blocked state says "Adding another employee seat costs 100 credits (≈ $29/mo) - top up credits or upgrade your plan to continue."
whyItsWrong: There is no recurring seat billing anywhere in the product. The seat charge happens exactly once, at the moment the seat is added, and no scheduled job ever charges it again. Presenting a single 100-credit debit as a monthly rate misstates the price in both directions: the client either expects to be billed again and isn't, or believes 100 credits buys a month of a seat when it buys the seat outright. It is a pricing claim the product cannot honour, shown at the exact moment the client decides to spend.

title: A task moved to "Review Pending" from the ticket vanishes from the board with no way back
surface: Workspace → Board → "Depending on you" tab → open an In Progress task → footer button
whatYouSee: On the "Depending on you" tab you open a task that is In Progress. The ticket footer offers "Move to Review Pending". You click it, the ticket closes, and the card is gone from the board. The tab counter still counts it, but there is no column, no filter setting and no drag target that can bring it back.
whyItsWrong: That tab deliberately shows only three columns because client-owned work is never supposed to sit in Review Pending, yet the ticket footer puts it there in one click. The card becomes unreachable: the status dropdown can filter to Review Pending but the column still is not rendered, so the count and the cards on screen disagree and it reads as if the work was deleted. It hits both the client's own Workspace and the staff Task Board, since both render the same board component.
fix: In src/components/task-ticket-modal.tsx stop reading the next status from the flat STATUS_NEXT map (line 33): when inferOwner(task) === "client_managed" (the helper already exists at line 69, and isClientManaged is already computed at line 526), in_progress must advance to "completed", skipping review_pending. Belt and braces: in src/lib/actions/task-actions.ts updateTaskStatusAction (line 70) reject status === "review_pending" when inferOwnerEngine(task) === "client_managed", and in src/components/tasks-board.tsx tasksByColumn (line 602) fold any client_managed review_pending task into the pending bucket while activeTab === "client" so already-stuck tasks resurface.

title: Branded "Connect with Instagram" buttons open a popup showing a bare error sentence, and only admins are told why
surface: Client Settings → Integrations (/clients/[id]/settings), also the onboarding socials step
whatYouSee: A client or employee clicks the full-colour "Connect with Instagram" (or Connect Google Suite) button. A popup opens containing one plain sentence on a blank white page: "OAuth not configured for this provider". The card behind it sits on "Connecting…" until the popup is closed by hand, then quietly reverts. No message ever appears in the app.
whyItsWrong: The Connect button is deliberately shown to everyone regardless of whether the server is configured, but the one line that explains the failure — "OAuth env vars not set. The button above will fail until configured." — is shown only to admins, so employees and clients never see it. And the authorization route answers its four failure cases with bare text bodies, while the app only listens for the structured success/failure messages the callback page sends. The failure therefore never reaches the app at all. Non-admins get a beautiful button whose entire behaviour is a blank popup.

title: Every client user can hand out permanent workspace access, and the key can never be rotated from the UI
whatYouSee: Any signed-in client user — not just their group admin — sees their workspace's invite key in plain text with a copy button and the line "Share this key with a teammate so they can join your workspace." Nowhere in the product is there a button to change that key.
whyItsWrong: That key auto-approves any new signup straight into the workspace as a linked client user, with no admin review — full access to that client's documents, assets, agents and credits. Once it leaks (pasted into a Slack channel, forwarded, screenshotted) there is no remediation path on screen: a regenerate action exists on the server and a panel component to drive it exists, but that panel is imported by no page — its only reference in the repo is its own file. So the rotate control is dead code and the key is effectively permanent. The Team page even documents this exact hazard about handing the key to a client component, and then the settings page shows it to every client user anyway.

title: The Autopilot switch spends the client's credits and fires five agent runs with no label, no price and no confirmation
whatYouSee: A bare toggle labelled "Autopilot off". No tooltip, no helper text, no price, no confirmation step. One click charges the client for up to five task executions and starts five agent runs. The only feedback is a red line if the charge is refused.

title: A task the platform then refuses still costs the client a credit
surface: AI Copilot panel → "Describe a task you need done… / Add" (and the same bar on the task board)
whatYouSee: Type a task, press Add, wait a couple of seconds, and get a red bar saying either that a similar task already exists on your board, or that the Karos AI queue is at capacity with fifteen active tasks. No task is created — and the credit balance in the left rail has gone down by one.
whyItsWrong: The charge is taken before both the capacity check and the duplicate check, and neither refusal path hands it back. The platform already has a refund mechanism, explicitly built so a failed run does not eat the weekly allowance, so charging for a refused write is an oversight rather than policy. It is also the one place a client can watch a credit disappear for nothing — and the duplicate case is dressed as an error when it is really information.
evidence: src/lib/actions/task-actions.ts:328-329 — chargeTaskAssist runs before anything is validated

Moving chargeTaskAssist below the checks is not equivalent — the Haiku routing call at line 346 has already cost real money by then and the title it produces is what the duplicate check needs — so refund, do not reorder. title: Adding a competitor from the sidebar does nothing visible when you are not on a client page
surface: Staff sidebar → COMPETITOR TRACK "+" quick-add, with a client selected but while on Dashboard, Settings, Assets, a job page or a meeting page
whatYouSee: With a client selected you click the plus next to COMPETITOR TRACK, type a name and hit Add. The spinner runs, "Analyzing competitor profile…" appears, the box closes with no error — and the list is unchanged. The competitor only appears once you navigate into that client's own pages.
whyItsWrong: The row is created and a model analysis of the whole tracked list is run and logged as usage, so retrying burns more spend each time and the person cannot tell whether the feature works. The staff sidebar reads its competitor list purely from in-browser context, and the only thing that refills that context lives in the client-page layout. On any other route that layout is not in the tree, so the refresh at the end of the add can never bring the new row back.
fix: Stop feeding the sidebar list from route-scoped context. Preferred: change addCompetitorByNameAction (src/lib/actions/competitor-actions.ts:461) to return the { company, created } it already computes from upsertManualCompetitor, and have CompetitorTrack (src/components/client-context-sections.tsx:80) append the row to local state on success — the same optimistic pattern handleRemove already uses with removedIds (line 54). Alternative: fetch competitors for the active client in src/app/(app)/layout.tsx and pass them into Sidebar as props so revalidatePath + router.refresh() actually re-render them. Either way, widen ClientContextSync's dependency list (src/lib/active-client-context.tsx:56) beyond competitors.length so a report-to-manual promotion, which leaves the count unchanged, still re-syncs.
